project.name: Distributed Anomaly Model Training Pipeline
bullets: Built a distributed training and batch-inference pipeline on Spark and Kubernetes for anomaly models over large telemetry datasets, parallelising feature engineering and PyTorch model training across worker nodes.
Evaluated models on holdout periods, tracked runs in MLflow, and deployed them to the cloud with Docker, adding alerts for drift and failed jobs.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Senior AI/ML Computational Scientist role. I am a senior AI engineer who has spent eight years turning business problems into production ML and LLM systems, lately in healthcare and before that in telecom networks. What connects it is the full lifecycle: understanding the data, choosing the model, and keeping it reliable once it is live.

Accenture puts AI into production for clients across many industries, and that variety is what drew me to consulting early in my career. My fiancée lives in Berlin, and we plan to move to Ireland together and settle there long term. Building a consulting career from Ireland fits that plan and the kind of client work I enjoy most.

I would bring production and client experience together. I prototyped 15+ AI applications for telecom clients, with 7 moving into production or paid work, and built an SLA breach prediction system with LightGBM and GPT-3.5 that reduced downtime by 67%. I am comfortable explaining those choices to engineers and business owners alike.

Outside work I am building ThinkTree.AI, a non-profit AI learning platform used by NGO teachers to support students with ADHD. It reminds me that a model is only useful when the people using it can trust it. I would be glad to discuss how I could help your clients.
